reviews.title: Greedy company
reviews.text:
I got the notification about the 69.99 charge and responded immediately. I didn’t use the trial and certainly would not invest in using a product that I stopped using almost as soon as I tried it. I had to dispute the transaction because the rep insisted that it was in their return policy and didn’t want to refund me.

I can’t imagine having a business, a customer tells me they barely used the trial for my product and admits that they have no intention of using my product, yet I want to take their money for a year anyways. How desperate and greedy. If I came a month late to the email asking for a refund, I’d understand completely. But I was under the impression that it was a 14 day trial and was not informed it was 69.99 for the year (I would never commit to a year regardless of cost). I contacted customer service 3 minutes after the charge notification came at 12:01am. I hate these predatory subscription models. They ought to be illegal and the customer should be required to sign off after the trial ends, otherwise, they just loose access to the product.

reviews.title: Add a library
reviews.text: Solo learn for me has been a very well done learning experience, but at certain points, it could start to feel a bit fast paced. I feel as though it would be a unique feature to add a “library”. Where it would act as a kind of dictionary that you progress through as you learn about the different functions and etc. As you go through lessons the library would update or unlock the terms you recently learned so its easy to go back to and find if you just forgot.

First lesson was fine. Dragging and dropping the bits of code doesn't work, but I can still tap them. I can live with that.

reviews.title: Beginner player unsatisfactory complaint
reviews.text: My only problem is that you have courses saying “Pro key level” in the middle of the game levels. You allow the players to play the game for free, but as they are playing, they run into  certain levels that require you to pay money to unlock . Problem is those levels are the important lessons they need for the next level. So if they aren’t able to pay, they miss an important part needed for the next level of the game. So I guess my recommendation is to either have a paid version or a totally free version or not let them pass on to the next level until they pay, which would discourage someone like me from playing and learning the coding skills. This needs to be improved.

reviews.title: It’s ok, but not for me
reviews.text: I downloaded this app because I was curious. I work in AI as a conversation designer so I tried the AI Agents for Beginners. It was fine at first. Very basic information that’s suitable for beginners. Then it basically threw me to the wolves with the Talking to the Model lesson and as someone who has very limited experience with Python, it was not helpful at all. I assumed the coding would be explained in some detail, but nope. It just assumed I knew what was going on. I wish there was a warning for needing to know Python beforehand. Also would be helpful to have documentation on the lessons just for people who want to dive a little deeper and have a more robust understanding of what they’re learning. I can see how this can be helpful for a lot of people, this just isn’t for me. I think I’m better off reading a book.
